clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau points to people who've had their blood drawn with a cholesterol count of 600, 700, even 800 - sky-high by any doctor's chart - who never develop heart disease and live to 90.

Meanwhile, plenty of people with very low counts still end up with fully blocked arteries.

His point: the number alone doesn't tell the whole story, yet a count of 240 is enough, by protocol, to write a prescription.

Worth asking what else your doctor is checking besides that one number.
